text:
The failing f_unity is the largest violation and points to the integrator time constant. R1 has the strongest sensitivity (-15.3% per +20%), and its value is about 17% below the ~16 kΩ needed to bring f_unity into band. Cf has a similar sensitivity, so it is the next candidate. M5 is also a plausible secondary cause: it is in triode, which explains the excess tail current and the power overage.

```json
{"ranking": ["R1", "M5", "Cf"], "fault": "R1 is undersized (13.33 kΩ, about 17% low; roughly 16 kΩ is needed). This sets the integrator gain 1/(R1·Cf) too high, pushing f_unity to 3.63 MHz versus the 2.68–3.28 MHz band. Raising R1 by about 20% should bring f_unity to about 3.07 MHz. Separately, the power overage (204.7 µW) is driven by M5 operating in triode, which lets the tail current exceed its mirror-set value (68 µA versus ~10 µA × mirror ratio)."}
```

Confidence is moderate. The power violation may be a design-level problem with M5 rather than the injected fault, and the sensitivity data alone cannot fully separate R1 from Cf.
